svg.text: SLANT measurement chain: from sunlight to thermospheric composition
Solar Limb Absorption of Neutrals in the Thermosphere. Panels 1–3 are what the instrument records, panel 4 is the primary data product, panel 5 is derived from it.
Geometry: solar occultation from a hosted payload
Reference ray: Sun above the atmosphere
As the Sun sets behind Earth's limb, the line of sight from the
Sun to the sensor descends through the thermosphere.
Tangent altitude zₜ: the lowest altitude a ray reaches.
Slant column N: molecules per cm² summed along the whole ray.
At most one occultation per orbit, at orbital sunset. Heights exaggerated; not to scale.
Instrument: five filtered slits, one detector
Zr, Al, In: metal foils about 0.2 µm thick, bonded to the plate. FUV1, FUV2: coated MgF₂
windows in holders. Slits 25 µm × 10 mm. Each slit forms a line image of the Sun, which
moves 2.8 mm down the rows as the Sun sets: row position gives Sun elevation, hence zₜ.
Rows are summed in 24 µm bins, 10 km of tangent altitude each. No moving parts.
Slit-to-channel order illustrative; not yet assigned.
Pale In bar: the measured indium film passes 100–122 nm light that O and N₂ do not absorb,
so below about 178 km τ stays near 1.3–2.7 and changes little with altitude.
I and I₀ come from the same detector rows in one occultation, so solar brightness cancels.
Beer's law: optical depth → slant column density
One equation per channel, with that channel's σ values. Optically thin form shown;
the retrieval uses the full band integral.
Solar-flux-weighted cross sections, optically thin. Zr, In: Luxel measured
films; Al, FUV: ideal bands. O and N₂ do not absorb above 115 nm in this
cross-section set, so FUV1 and FUV2 measure O₂ alone. Because the channels
weight the three species differently, the five equations fix three columns.

text.tspan: slant columns of O, N₂ and O₂ at each tangent altitude, with their error budget.

svg.text: Beer's law only; no atmospheric model enters this step.
Inversion: slant columns → local density and temperature
Each ray crosses its own tangent shell and every shell above it.
Solving from the top shell down (onion peel), or fitting a
few-parameter profile, converts N(zₜ) into local density n(z).
For a layer with scale height H:
N / n: effective path length, larger for species with a larger H.

text.tspan: n(z) for O, N₂, O₂ and T(z), each reported with its dependence on the assumed profile shape.

svg.text: 10 km sampling; effective vertical resolution of order one scale height.
optical depth τ = −ln(I/I₀) in each channel at each tangent altitude

Curves computed 27 Sep 2026 with channel-plan/occ.py and filters_measured.py (workflow_data.py): NRLMSIS 2.1, F10.7 = 140, ap = 4, equinox, equator, the simulator's quiet truth atmosphere, which also stands in for a retrieved profile in panel 5.
Zr and In use Luxel's measured film curves (18 Sep 2026, digitized, about ±10 % in band); Al and both FUV channels are ideal top-hat bands. Panels 1 and 2 are schematic.
